latest_inference.note: The candidates remain the same as the previous list. The patient reports a distinct period of 8 months with elevated mood, irritability, decreased need for sleep, and impulsive spending causing major relationship problems. These symptoms strongly suggest a manic or hypomanic episode. While the duration (8 months) and severity (major relationship problems) are concerning for Mania (Bipolar I), the absence of explicit mention of psychosis or hospitalization means Bipolar II (hypomania) and Major Depressive Disorder (given the reported 'empty and deeply sad' periods) remain viable differential diagnoses until further clarification on the exact functional impairment level and presence of psychotic features is obtained.

Major Depressive Disorder is included as a differential until the severity and duration of the 'high' periods can be confirmed to distinguish between hypomania (Bipolar II) and mania (Bipolar I), or to rule out the presence of a manic episode entirely.
